candidates.evidence: Two strong non-substrate modes at about 206 and 472 cm-1 on SiO2/Si, consistent with a layered FeOCl-type (Pmmn) Ti-N/Ti-Cl compound. The assignment rests on rough recollection of the literature, which I could not check. Two peaks alone are not unique.
The same layered structure type gives Raman modes in the 200-500 cm-1 range. The reported lines (about 215, 300, 400 for CrOCl) do not match 206/472 well.
Ti-chalcogenide layered compound. Its Eg/A1g modes (about 230/330 cm-1) do not match the observed 206/472 lines.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was given in the metadata (material_hint is null), so this is an identification from the spectrum alone.

limits: The data are noisy: baseline about 3400 counts, noise rms about 500. Only the 206 and 472 cm-1 modes and the Si 520.5 cm-1 line are clearly significant. All other weak features have SNR of about 3 or less.

No cosmic-ray spikes were found in the data (a deviation test on a smoothed trace found none). The weak features at 234, 323, 403 and 686 cm-1 may be noise, Si second-order structure, or genuine weak modes.

The TiNCl identification rests on two modes and a recalled literature comparison. I could not check reference spectra, and other layered MOCl-type or nitride-halide compounds are not strictly excluded.
No polarization or angle data were available, so the mode symmetries (Ag, B2g, B3g) are tentative and no polarization pattern is assigned.
Layer number, strain and doping cannot be inferred from this spectrum.
The Lorentzian fit parameters of the weak peaks were poorly constrained and some fit widths hit their bounds. FWHM values are rough.
